entity: Sardar Sarovar Dam (SSNNL) release
location: Narmada river downstream of Sardar Sarovar Dam
finding: Release started 16 Sep and rose to 17.42 lakh cusecs by 4 am 17 Sep against inflow of 19.53 lakh cusecs; dam 99.93% full
source_quote: Water release from Narmada dam started at noon on September 16 in the size of 1.45 lakh cusecs but gradually it increased to 17.42 lakh cusecs as of 4 a.m. on September 17, against an inflow of 19.53 lakh cusecs.
notes: DeshGujarat says release began at noon on 16 Sep (1.45 lakh cusecs); task brief says 10 am. SANDRP (next row) says no gates opened till 10 am, releases only after that, 1600 cumecs by 1200 hrs.

entity: Sardar Sarovar Dam (SSNNL) release timing
finding: No gate opened till 10 am on 16 Sep; releases after that rose to 1600 cumecs by 1200 hrs and 11500 cumecs by 1500 hrs
source_quote: till 10 am on Sept 16, shockingly, SSP authorities had still not opened any of the gates, the releases were only from River Bed Power House (RBPH) and Canal Head Power House (CHPH), amounting to total of less than 400 cumecs
notes: SANDRP is an advocacy analysis of CWC data, not an SSNNL statement; treat as third-party interpretation.

entity: Sardar Sarovar Dam peak outflow
finding: Peak release about 52706 cumecs (18.76 lakh cusecs) by 0500 hrs on 17 Sep, held at high level for several hours
source_quote: lead to the SSP authorities having to release upto 52706 cumecs (18.76 lakh cusecs) by 0500 hrs on Sept 17 and then maintaining at around that high level for several hours thereafter.
notes: Later SANDRP article (b5 source) cites CWC peak outflow 18.61 lakh cusecs at 0500 hrs; figures differ by source.

entity: Sardar Sarovar Dam peak inflow
finding: Peak inflow 63950 cumecs at 0100 hrs 17 Sep; SANDRP says this exceeded the 50-year flood
source_quote: The inflows into SSP reached 63950 cumecs (22.58 lakh cusecs) by 0100 hrs on Sept 17, 2023.

entity: Narmada river level at Golden Bridge, Bharuch
finding: Golden Bridge level crossed danger mark of 24 ft after 4.30 am and was above 25 ft and rising at 5 am
source_quote: The water level at Golden Bridge which is located between Bharuch and Ankleshwar over river Narmada has crossed the danger mark of 24 ft post 4.30 am. As of 5 am, the level is above 25 ft and rising speedily.

entity: Narmada river level at Golden Bridge, Bharuch
finding: Level 32.38 ft at 12 noon on 17 Sep; expected to reach 40 ft; outflow from dam at noon 18.35 lakh cusecs
source_quote: At 12 noon today, the level of water at Golden bridge in Bharuch was 32.38 ft, well above the danger mark of 24 ft.

entity: Narmada river level at Golden Bridge, Bharuch
finding: SANDRP reports peak water level of 12.34 m at Golden Bridge (about 40.5 ft by simple conversion, not stated in source)
source_quote: with actual peak water level of 12.34 m attained at Golden Bridge in Bharuch (see the hydrograph for Bharuch above), the flow would be 65000 cumecs or 22.95 lakh cusecs
notes: Level given in metres in source; feet conversion is mine. SANDRP also notes flow implied by SSNNL flood memorandum is higher than CWC release figure.

entity: Narmada river level, Ankleshwar-Bharuch
finding: Narmada level reached 42 ft on night of 17 Sep per local reporting
source_quote: Water started flowing in the town on 17 September morning, but the levels increased during the night when the level of water of river Narmada went up to 42 ft.
notes: Gauge location not specified in the article.

entity: Gujarat government explanation of cause
finding: Gujarat govt spokesperson said Omkareshwar release rose to 4.53 lakh cusecs and Sardar Sarovar inflow went from 5.31 lakh to 22 lakh cusecs; Congress alleged 18.2 lakh cusecs release
source_quote: Patel said, at water release from Omkareshwar was increased from 68,000 cusecs to 4.53 lakh cusecs at 3 am. After 8 to 12 hours travel, the waters arrived at Sardar Sarovar dam with additional water of fresh rains on the route.
notes: Political dispute; Congress called it man-made, govt refuted.

entity: Sardar Sarovar River Bed Power House idle
finding: No generation at 1200 MW RBPH from 6 to 16 Sep, which SANDRP says would have reduced peak outflow if run
source_quote: there was no power generation at the 1200 MW River Bed Power House (RBPH) of the SSP from Sept 6 to Sept 16. This not only means loss of power generation of about 270 million units (MU)
notes: Not a downstream power outage; relevant only for cause of flood.

entity: Ankleshwar (industrial town; GIDC not named)
finding: Ankleshwar under water up to first floor; shops and parked vehicles heavily damaged; no plant or GIDC estate named
source_quote: The industrial town of Ankleshwar is under water up to the first floor. Thousands of vehicles across the town are in the water.
notes: Article says level started to fall slowly on afternoon of 18 Sep. Source describes the town, not specific factories; do not read as plant-level evidence.

entity: Ankleshwar residential societies (Hansot Road, Diva Road)
finding: Residential societies on Ankleshwar-Hansot road flooded to 10-15 ft; Hansot and Diva Road societies 15-20 ft
source_quote: Ankleshwar’s Hansot Road and Diva Road residential societies and flats suffered the brunt of the floods, with water levels reaching a remarkable 15 to 20 feet.
notes: Residential, not industrial. Included only to show depth of flooding around Ankleshwar.

entity: Bharuch and Narmada districts (business and industry, unspecified)
finding: SANDRP: huge impacts on business, industries, houses; 216 villages in 4 talukas affected; no unit names
source_quote: There are huge impacts on business, industries, people’s houses, and lives in general.
notes: Generic statement without named units or rupee value.

entity: Western Railway Mumbai-Ahmedabad line, Narmada bridge no. 502 (Bharuch-Ankleshwar)
finding: Train operations halted about 12 hours when Narmada rose above danger mark at bridge 502; all passenger and goods trains held at both ends
source_quote: The operation of trains on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad route between Bharuch and Ankleshwar stations under the Vadodara division stopped after Narmada river waters surged above the danger mark at brigade no. 502 at around 11:50 pm on Sunday.
notes: Resumption slowly at about 11:30 am Monday 18 Sep per Western Railway Chief PRO. Goods trains also held, relevant for dispatch from Ankleshwar/Dahej belt.

entity: Golden Bridge, Narmada Maiya Bridge, Silver Bridge, Bharuch-Ankleshwar road and NH
finding: Golden, Narmada Maiya and Silver bridges closed; first rail disruption since 2013; 1-2 km traffic jam on national highway
source_quote: ગોલ્ડન બ્રિજ, નર્મદામૈયા બ્રિજ બાદ સિલ્વર બ્રિજ પણ બંધ કરાયો છે.
notes: English gloss: After Golden Bridge and Narmada Maiya Bridge, Silver Bridge has also been closed. Same article: rail traffic hit for the first time since 2013; Bharuch-Ankleshwar road closed causing 1-2 km jam on national highway; 15+ Mumbai-Ahmedabad trains cancelled.

entity: NH 48 and Narmada bridge, Bharuch
finding: District collector closed the Narmada bridge and advised commuters to use NH 48 between Bharuch and Ankleshwar, so NH 48 itself was not reported closed here
source_quote: Commuters have been advised by the district collector’s office to use National Highway 48 for travel between Bharuch and Ankleshwar.
notes: Article date 19 Sep 2023; no evidence found of NH 48 closure in 2023.

entity: Power supply in flood-affected Bharuch/Narmada villages (DGVCL/MGVCL not named)
finding: Power supply restored in more than 230 flood-affected villages in Central Gujarat by night, after water receded
source_quote: The power supply was restored in more than 230 flood-affected villages in Central Gujarat till night.
notes: The AIR page shows no date in the reader text; context (Bharuch and Narmada flood, 100 percent seasonal rainfall) matches Sep 2023 but date should be checked. No outage start date or industrial feeders given.

entity: Gujarat government farmer package for Narmada flood
finding: Special crop relief package for farmers in three districts, in addition to SDRF norms
source_quote: The Gujarat government on Saturday announced a special relief package for farmers hit by an overflowing Narmada river in Bharuch, Narmada and Vadodara districts between September 16 and September 18.
notes: Agriculture only, not industry.

entity: Gujarat government traders/shops package after Narmada flood
location: Bharuch, Vadodara, Narmada (40 villages and 2 cities of Bharuch, 31 villages of Vadodara, 32 villages of Narmada)
finding: Cash aid for lorries, cabins and shops; Rs 85,000 for small/medium pucca shops; interest subsidy on loan up to Rs 20 lakh for big shops; no industry/MSME unit scheme in this notice
source_quote: Small and medium units with pucca shops, having monthly turnover of up to Rs 5 lakh (as per GST return), will be getting Rs 85,000.
notes: KNN page updated 30 Sep 2023. Covers shops and cabins, not factories.

entity: Gujarat cabinet relief for trade and commerce units
location: Narmada, Bharuch, Vadodara, Dahod, Panchmahal, Anand, Aravalli, Banaskantha, Mahisagar
finding: Cabinet decided relief for nine rain-affected districts; Rs 5,000 for small carts, Rs 20,000 / 40,000 for cabins, Rs 85,000 for small and medium shops
source_quote: Small and medium-sized brick-and-mortar shops, with a monthly turnover up to ₹5 lakh (according to GST returns), will get an aid of ₹85,000.
notes: Same package as previous row, second source.

entity: Estimated damage in Bharuch and Narmada districts (SANDRP citing a Gujarati news report)
finding: Estimated damage in two districts at least Rs 3000 crore; crops destroyed over about 3 lakh ha (secondary, unverified)
source_quote: the estimated damage in two districts of Bharuch and Narmada is at least Rs 3000 crores due to the floods. Farmers of some 214 villages have seen destruction of their crops over some 3 lakh ha.
notes: SANDRP cites a watchgujarat.com report, which I did not read; treat figure as unverified and mostly agricultural.

entity: Vadodara rainfall and Vishwamitri flood height
finding: About 12.44 inches rain in Vadodara and 7.51 inches in Halol on 26 Aug; 37 ft Vishwamitri flood, above 2005, 2014, 2019 floods
source_quote: Extremely heavy rainfall of around 12.44 inches in Vadodara coupled with very heavy rainfall of 7.51 inches in Halol on August 26 brought flood to the city of Vadodara. This was a 37 ft height flood
notes: DeshGujarat explainer published 1 Oct 2024.

entity: Ajwa and Pratappura reservoir releases
finding: VMC opened 62 gates of Ajwa dam at noon 24 Aug releasing 1540 cusecs per hour, before the main rain on 26 Aug
source_quote: opened 62 gates of Ajwa dam at 12 noon on 24th itself to release 1540 cusecs/hour water when Ajwa level was at 211.65 ft.

entity: Vadodara flood duration
finding: City under water for nearly 72 hours after 9.4 inches (239 mm) rain in 24 hours on 26-27 Aug
source_quote: After receiving almost 9.4 inches (239 mm) of rain in 24 hours from August 26 and 27, causing the 134-year-old Ajwa and the 94-year-old Pratappura reservoirs to overflow and flood the Vishwamitri river
notes: Photo caption quoted by SANDRP, originally Indian Express; the rainfall number differs from DeshGujarat (12.44 in) because of different gauge and window.

entity: GE T&D India (Vadodara plant; not in sample list)
finding: Company reported Vadodara plant operations disrupted by heavy rain and water logging; loss under insurance, amount after survey
source_name: Business Standard (capital market news, relaying a company disclosure)
source_quote: operations at the company's Plant situated at Vadodara, Gujarat, have been disrupted due to heavy rain fall & water logging.
notes: Business Standard relays a stock-exchange disclosure, so this is company-sourced reporting; included as the only named industrial plant found for 2024. No restart date given.

entity: Vadodara industrial workers (INTUC Vadodara)
finding: Union says many labourers could not attend work for four to five days due to flooding; demanded absent days be counted as present
source_quote: many labourers could not attend work for four to five days due to the flooding, resulting in wage losses.
notes: Union claim, not a plant-level or estate-level count; no estate named.

entity: Industrial units drawn on for flood clean-up (Vadodara)
finding: Minister directed collection of JCBs and dumper trucks from nearby industrial units for municipal clean-up (units not named)
source_quote: Sanghavi said instructions are given to collect JCBs and dumper trucks from nearby industrial units and add them to the strength of VMC for cleaning work post-flood.
notes: Implies some industrial equipment was usable; no estate named.

entity: Vadodara power feeders (MGVCL, not named in text)
finding: 118 feeders shut during waterlogging, only 12 still shut by 29 Aug; restoration by midnight where water cleared
source_quote: About power supply, Sanghavi said 118 feeders were shut during waterlogging; out of them, only 12 feeders are shut now.
notes: Another outlet reported 68 feeders and 365 transformers shut; that page could not be read (404), so not used.

entity: Vadodara electricity restoration
finding: MoS Home said 99% of electricity restoration completed as of 2 Sep
source_quote: The agricultural survey work commenced this morning, and 99% of electricity restoration has been completed.

entity: Western Railway Vadodara division, Bajva station and bridge 561
finding: Waterlogging at Bajva station on 27 Aug led to 12 trains cancelled; 16 more cancelled on 28 Aug due to bridge 561 waterlogging
source_quote: Western Railway cancelled 16 trains on Wednesday due to severe water logging in the Vadodara division. Earlier 12 trains were cancelled on Tuesday due to waterlogging at Bajva station.
notes: Article dated 28 Aug 2024. Freight impact not stated.

entity: Western Railway Vadodara division train disruption (first day)
finding: Waterlogging at Bajva station affected trains on 26 Aug: cancellations, short-terminations
source_quote: As per the Divisional Railway Manager of Vadodara Division, due to heavy rains and subsequent waterlogging at Bajva Station, Vadodara Division, the following trains are affected:

entity: Dahej port terminals
finding: Dahej port suspended berthing operations at several terminals on 29 Aug due to heavy rainfall and wind, then resumed
source_quote: Dahej port has also resumed operations after suspending berthing operations at several terminals due to heavy rainfall and wind on 29 August.
notes: ICIS cites GAC note dated 2 Sep. Terminals not named, so cannot be tied to Petronet LNG. Weather (rain and wind), not river flood.

entity: Insurers in Vadodara (4 public sector, private)
finding: About 850 claims with four government insurers and about 650 with private insurers as of 2 Sep; insurers told to process on humanitarian grounds
source_quote: Approximately 850 claims have been made with four government insurance companies, and around 650 claims have been submitted to private companies.
notes: Mostly household and vehicle claims; no General Insurance Council aggregate or industrial claim figure found.

entity: Vehicle claims in Vadodara
finding: Over 25 insurers processing flood claims; more than 10,000 vehicles affected; 25-30% of submerged cars likely irreparable
source_quote: Initial reports indicate that more than 10,000 vehicles were affected, leading to extensive damage.
notes: Same article: 25% to 30% of submerged cars likely irreparable; over 25 insurers processing claims.

entity: Gujarat Vadodara traders package
finding: State package: Rs 5,000 lorries, Rs 20,000/40,000 cabins, Rs 85,000 pucca shops; loan relief for turnover above Rs 5 lakh; total outlay not disclosed
source_quote: Although the government has not disclosed the total financial outlay of the relief package, Patel emphasised that the funds will be disbursed from the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund (CMRF).
notes: Page shows updated Sep 13, 2024. Shops and cabins, not factories.

entity: Early disbursal to Vadodara traders
finding: 3,555 traders paid Rs 5.25 crore so far; Rs 25 crore allocated; Rs 3 crore to 752 large cabin traders, Rs 25.5 lakh to 30 permanent-shop traders
source_quote: Small traders affected by the recent floods in Vadodara have received direct financial aid of ₹5.25 crore from the state government so far.

entity: Vadodara flood relief, businesses and households
finding: Rs 100 crore state allocation, 75% to Vadodara; Rs 74.37 crore disbursed; 12,027 flood-affected businesses received Rs 23.31 crore
source_quote: 12,027 flood-affected businesses received Rs 23.31 crore in compensation, a significant step towards helping local businesses recover from the disaster,
notes: Official quoted by IANS.

entity: Gujarat request to Centre for MSME production loss (Rajya Sabha reply by MoS MSME)
finding: Gujarat reported 958 industrial units affected by heavy rains this monsoon and sought Rs 36.81 crore for production losses to MSMEs in Vadodara district
source_quote: The request for compensation, amounting to Rs 36.81 crore, is for production losses caused by the heavy rains and floods that particularly impacted MSMEs in Vadodara district.
notes: Article text gives 958 units; its headline says Rs 3.68 billion, same as 36.81 crore. Year not printed in article text; 2024 inferred from Sep 2024 Vadodara package reference. Official Rajya Sabha text could not be read (fetch refused). Request, not an approved amount.

entity: Central team assessment
finding: Home Ministry set up an Inter-Ministerial Central Team led by NIDM Executive Director to assess damage from 25-30 Aug rain and floods
source_quote: The Union Home Ministry has constituted an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) led by the Executive Director, National Institute of Disaster Management, to assess damages caused by rainfall and floods in Gujarat.
notes: Date taken from the search listing for this AIR page, not shown in reader text. A search snippet of a Dec 2024 Rajya Sabha reply said Gujarat had not submitted a memorandum with a loss estimate; I could not open that PDF, so it is not recorded as a fact.

entity: Centre approval of advance relief
finding: Centre approved Rs 600 crore for Gujarat from NDRF advance (Rs 675 crore across Gujarat, Manipur, Tripura)
source_quote: Of the total amount, 600 crore rupees have been approved for Gujarat, 50 crore rupees for Manipur and 25 crore rupees for Tripura.
notes: Disaster relief, not industry loss. Date from search listing title.

entity: Named plants of sample firms (GNFC Bharuch, UPL Ankleshwar/Jhagadia/Dahej, Aarti Industries, DCM Shriram, Borosil Renewables, SRF Dahej, MRF Dahej, Reliance Dahej, GAIL Gandhar, NTPC Jhanor-Gandhar, ONGC Ankleshwar, Petronet LNG Dahej, Kiri, Bodal)
finding: No third-party report found naming any sample-firm plant as flooded, shut, or restarted because of the Sep 2023 Narmada flood
notes: Queries: "Dahej industries Bharuch flood Narmada September 2023 plants Dahej port"; "Bharuch Ankleshwar flood September 2023 industries units damaged Dahej Panoli GIDC power cut NH48"; "GSFC OR GNFC OR Gujarat Alkalies flood September 2023 plant"; "Dahej port OR Petronet LNG flood September 2023". Results were about the town, bridges and dam only.

entity: Ankleshwar GIDC, Panoli, Jhagadia and Dahej estates; Ankleshwar Industries Association, Panoli Industries Association, Dahej Industries Association statements
finding: No 2023 statement found from any industries association on units flooded, days lost or rupee loss; search returns were 2004-2007 floods, a 2026 gas-supply story, or an undated Dahej effluent pipeline story
notes: Queries: "Ankleshwar GIDC industries flooded Narmada September 2023 loss crore Ankleshwar Industries Association"; "Ankleshwar Panoli industries flood 2023 units shut power supply ..."; an extended-mode "Ankleshwar flood 2023 Industries Association OR GIDC production halted" search; Gujarati query on Ankleshwar GIDC Narmada flood industries closed. Older stories (Business Standard 2004-2007, Down To Earth) deliberately excluded because they are different floods.

entity: Apollo Tyres Limda (Vadodara); CEAT Halol; IOC Gujarat Refinery
finding: No flood-related stoppage found. Apollo Limda halt of 20-24 Sep 2023 appeared in search but was a labour matter, not flood
notes: Query: "Apollo Tyres Limda Vadodara plant flood August 2024" returned search snippets about a Sep 2023 Limda stoppage described as labour-related (I did not open those pages). The labour halt is not a flood effect and should not be coded as one.

entity: Insurers / General Insurance Council claims for Narmada flood
finding: No insurer or GIC statement on claims from the Sep 2023 flood found
notes: Queries: the Bharuch/Dahej/Ankleshwar flood-impact searches above (none returned an insurer statement); no dedicated 2023 insurance query was run. An Asia Insurance Post link appeared in one result list but was not opened.

entity: Gujarat Pollution Control Board closure/restart orders tied to flood
finding: No GPCB or factory-inspectorate order tied to the 2023 flood found. GPCB items found (closure direction 14 Dec 2023 for coloured effluent in Ankleshwar GIDC storm drain; letter of 29 Sep 2023 on discharges) are pollution matters, not flood orders
notes: Query: "Gujarat Pollution Control Board flood Vadodara OR Ankleshwar closure direction industries restart after flood 2024 OR 2023". The GPCB items were an NGT action-taken report seen only as a search snippet.

entity: MGVCL/DGVCL industrial feeder suspension and restoration times; NH 48 closure; Dahej port disruption
finding: No feeder-level power outage data, no NH 48 closure and no Dahej port disruption found for Sep 2023 (Dahej monsoon rules only)
notes: Queries: "Bharuch Narmada flood September 2023 power supply DGVCL restored feeders"; "Dahej port ... flood September 2023". Narmada bridge closure with NH 48 left open is recorded separately.

entity: Central team assessment / loss memorandum for Sep 2023 flood and industry or MSME breakdown
finding: No central team report or industry breakdown found; only farmer and trader packages
notes: Queries: "Dahej industries Bharuch flood Narmada September 2023..." and "Gujarat government relief package Vadodara flood 2024 ... MSME" (which also surfaced the 2023 packages). India TV article on SIT demand and compensation returned HTTP 403 via reader and was not read.

entity: Named plants of sample firms (Gujarat Alkalies, GSFC Vadodara, IOC Gujarat Refinery Koyali, Reliance Vadodara, Apollo Tyres Limda/Waghodia, CEAT Halol, GAIL, UPL, GNFC, SRF, MRF, Aarti, DCM Shriram)
finding: No third-party report found of any sample-firm plant being flooded, stopped or restarted in the Aug 2024 floods
notes: Queries: "Vadodara flood 2024 Gujarat Refinery Koyali OR Reliance Vadodara OR Apollo Tyres OR GSFC OR Gujarat Alkalies operations flood"; "Apollo Tyres Limda Vadodara plant flood August 2024"; "GSFC OR Gujarat Alkalies Vadodara flood August 2024". IOC Koyali results were the Nov 2024 benzene tank fire, not flood. A 2019 GSFC power-interruption shutdown appeared and was excluded as a different event.

entity: VCCI, FGI, GCCI statements; Makarpura, Nandesari, Waghodia, Savli, Halol, Padra estates
finding: No statement found from VCCI, Federation of Gujarat Industries or GCCI, and no report naming units flooded or days lost in Makarpura, Nandesari, Waghodia, Savli, Halol or Padra
notes: Queries: "Vadodara flood August 2024 industries loss crore VCCI Makarpura GIDC Nandesari"; "Vadodara flood August 2024 industrial estates Makarpura Waghodia Savli Halol factories closed workers VCCI loss"; Gujarati query on Vadodara flood industries loss VCCI Makarpura GIDC. Other sources found (GE T&D, INTUC) recorded above.

entity: Gujarat Pollution Control Board / factory inspectorate closure or restart orders tied to the flood
finding: No flood-related GPCB or inspectorate order found; GPCB results were unrelated pollution closures
notes: Query: "Gujarat Pollution Control Board flood Vadodara OR Ankleshwar closure direction industries restart after flood 2024 OR 2023" (search snippets only).

entity: General Insurance Council or insurer aggregate claim value for Vadodara flood
finding: No aggregate claim value in rupees and no GIC statement found; only claim counts (about 1,500) and vehicle numbers (recorded above)
notes: Query: "Vadodara floods insurance claims General Insurance Council OR insurers claims crore August 2024".

entity: NH 48 closure and Vadodara-area highway status
finding: No source found confirming an NH 48 closure in Aug 2024; rail disruption is recorded above
notes: Query: "Gujarat heavy rain August 2024 NH48 Vadodara closed railway cancelled trains".

entity: Petronet LNG Dahej terminal and Dahej/Panoli/Ankleshwar estates in Aug 2024
finding: No report of flooding or outage at the Petronet Dahej terminal or at Panoli/Ankleshwar estates in Aug 2024; only the Dahej port berthing suspension on 29 Aug (recorded above)
notes: Queries: "Dahej port OR Petronet LNG OR Dahej SEZ OR Reliance Dahej flood September 2023 ..." (returned the 29 Aug 2024 port item); Ankleshwar 2024 was not searched separately. Ankleshwar gas-supply cut story found is from March 2026, unrelated.
